commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. Do NOT use for read-only questions about a Google file, or for Word, Excel, PowerPoint or PDF files. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill. commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. I booked one appointment: Dr. Morgan Reyes, 3:00 PM, Telehealth, half-hour video visit.

**Choosing the slot.** I read every listing in the Clinic Slots window (Chrome for Testing, window 69206) and ruled out the rest:
- **Too early or wrong length:** the 1:30 PM slot is 60 minutes, 1:45 PM starts before 2:00, 2:30 PM is 45 minutes, and 11:00 AM is before 2:00.
- **Not Dr. Morgan Reyes:** 2:00 PM is Morgan Lee, NP, 2:05 PM is Dr. Alan Morgan, 2:15 PM is Dr. Priya Shah (covering for Reyes), 2:20 PM is Dr. Kim Ortega, and 2:45 PM is Dr. Morgan Reyes**ford**.
- **Valid but later:** 3:15 PM and 4:00 PM.
- **Earliest valid:** the 3:00 PM Telehealth slot, listed as "half-hour" rather than "30 min". I counted it as a 30-minute appointment. If you meant in-person visits only, the next match is 3:15 PM, and I'd need to undo this booking first.

**What I did.** I scrolled the list down inside that window and clicked the Book button on the 3:00 PM card once. I touched no other window, tab or app.

**Verification.** After the click, the page showed "Booked: Dr. Morgan Reyes, half-hour, 3:00 PM". I confirmed this in a screenshot and by reading the page text through the accessibility tree. The automated postcondition check (`verify_state`) returned "unknown", so the screenshot and page text are my evidence. I didn't click anything else, so only one booking was made.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The listings had traps: a similar name ("Reyesford"), a covering doctor, a 45-minute slot, and a half-hour entry worded differently. Filtering on each criterion separately is safer than skimming for "Reyes".
- The first accessibility snapshot only held the top of the page. After scrolling I re-read the window and used a pixel click, because the truncated tree had no usable element token for the Book button.
- The click's own result was marked "unverifiable". The page's confirmation text was the evidence, not the click's success message.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
